newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank state debt trade hit 1.1 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: China interbank state debt trade hit 1.1 bln yuan.

text.p: The first day of trading of state debt on China's interbank market on Monday went smoothly, with turnover hitting 1.1 billion yuan, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.

Beijing in early June banned all state banks from trading state debt spot and repurchase contracts on the nation's securities exchanges and trading centres, ordering them to shift their positions to the Chinese yuan interbank market.
On Monday, the People's Bank (central bank) issued a circular saying all state banks could now start trading their state debt positions on the interbank market.

"The first day of trading in state debt by state banks on the interbank market went smoothly with the market's computerised system working well," the newspaper said. "This has laid the foundation for the further development of interbank debt trading."

A total of 23 of the 27 designated state banks on the market traded on Monday with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China the biggest player, trading 800 million yuan in 14-day state debt repurchase contracts, the newspaper said.
The market trades three state debt spot contracts and seven state debt repo contracts, the newspaper said.
